patterns: how do i become a lawyer
entries.answer: A law degree teaches how to reason about rules and how to apply them to facts nobody has seen before, which is the part that transfers to work outside law as well. In the Philippines the bachelor of laws is four years of study and a further year of practical training before the integration exam, and the graduate is then called a lawyer even before practising. The course is heavy on reading and writing, and the writing is the part that is underestimated.

entries.answer: A case brief is a structured summary of a decided case, and the structure is the point rather than the length. The standard parts are the facts, the issue, the rule, the holding and the reasoning, in that order, and a brief that cannot state the issue in one sentence has not understood it. Doing them repeatedly is how the reading converts into usable skill, since the discipline is separating what a court decided from what somebody afterwards said about it.

patterns: difference between statute and common law
entries.answer: A statute is a law passed by a legislature, and the word distinguishes it from a case, which is a decision a court made. In common-law systems both are binding, and the relationship is that a statute overrides an inconsistent earlier decision. Legislation is also easier to amend, since a legislature can change it, which is why detailed rules end up there and general principles end up in judgments.

patterns: why do lawyers do pro bono
entries.answer: Pro bono means done without charge, and in law it describes work given free to somebody who cannot pay, usually with an expectation of court costs being reduced. The term has broadened outside law to any unpaid professional work, sometimes with the board serving the community rather than the client. It is also a route into practice, since the experience counts and the exposure is real, though it is unpaid and the hours are often unglamorous.
